Apply the uniform styling inputs to a module's figure

Source: R/plot_tiers.R
apply_uniform_styling.Rd

The plot modules build their figures in two steps. The first draws the plot itself from the data and every input that changes what is drawn; that is the expensive part (a ggplot built and converted with plotly::ggplotly(), say), and it is cached. This function is the second step: it applies the inputs that only style the figure – titles, fonts, ticks and their notation, gridlines, the padding around the data, reference lines, the modebar, the shape-drawing tool, and the legend – to the figure the first step returned. Changing one of those inputs re-runs only this step, which takes a few milliseconds rather than a full rebuild.

Usage

apply_uniform_styling(
  fig,
  input,
  isolate_fn = isolate,
  facet.by = NULL,
  title_y = 0.95,
  include.modebar.buttons = TRUE,
  fig.fn = NULL,
  ggplot.axis.styling = TRUE,
  legend.position = NULL,
  padding.axes = c("x", "y")
)

Arguments

fig

A plotly figure: the module's plot, before styling.

input

The module's Shiny input, holding the uniform inputs from uniform_axes_inputs_ui(), uniform_lines_inputs_ui(), uniform_plotly_inputs_ui(), and uniform_legend_inputs_ui().

isolate_fn

The function from setup_auto_update_logic() that every input read goes through.

facet.by

The facetting column(s), or NULL. A faceted figure has shared axis titles drawn as annotations, which are styled to match, and no main title (see add_plot_config()).

title_y

Vertical position of the main title, in paper coordinates.

include.modebar.buttons

Passed to add_plot_config().

fig.fn

Optional function(fig, input, isolate_fn) returning the figure, run after the legend is styled and before the axis titles become draggable annotations, so any axis title text it sets is the one made draggable. Read inputs in it as isolate_fn(input$key). It runs after any overlay panels are drawn, so anything it places on "paper" coordinates can land on them; use xref = "x domain" and yref = "y domain" to stay within the plot's panel.

ggplot.axis.styling

Passed to create_axis_styles(). TRUE for a figure whose axis lines come from its ggplot theme (see create_ggplot_axis_style()); FALSE sets them from the Axes inputs here.

legend.position

Passed to apply_legend_inputs(); NULL keeps the legend where it is.

padding.axes

Which of the module's axes, "x" and "y", take the axis.padding.x/axis.padding.y inputs (see apply_axis_padding()). Leave out an axis with its own limit inputs, so its limits stand. When input$rotate is TRUE the padding follows the variables onto the swapped axes.

Value

The styled plotly figure.

Details

The figure passed in is never modified (R copies on write), so each call styles the cached figure afresh and nothing appended here (reference lines, say) accumulates across calls.

Axes used only by overlay panels drawn alongside the plot (the scatter plot's marginal distributions, see add_marginal_plots()) keep their own styling and get no reference lines.

See also

apply_title_layout(), apply_subplot_axis_styling(), apply_tick_notation(), apply_axis_padding(), add_reference_lines(), add_plot_config(), apply_plotly_newshape(), apply_legend_inputs(), axis_titles_as_annotations()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

fig <- plotly::plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers")
# The uniform inputs, as a module's `input` would hold them.
input <- list(
    title.font.size = 20, title.font.family = "Arial", title.font.color = "#000000",
    axis.title.horizontal.position = 0.5, axis.title.font.size = 16,
    axis.title.font.family = "Arial", axis.title.font.color = "#000000",
    axis.tickfont.size = 12, axis.tickfont.family = "Arial", axis.tickfont.color = "#000000",
    axis.tickangle.x = 0, axis.tickangle.y = 0, axis.ticks = "outside",
    axis.tickcolor = "#000000", axis.ticklen = 5, axis.tickwidth = 1,
    show.grid.x = TRUE, show.grid.y = FALSE, grid.color = "#CCCCCC",
    hline.intercepts = "20", hline.colors = "#D55E00",
    download.format = "svg", legend.text.size = 12, legend.title.size = 14
)
apply_uniform_styling(fig, input, isolate_fn = identity)
